title: rho_s definition does not match Background; classical reduction overstated

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: minor (mismatch with the Background definition / overstated reduction).**

The Background defines $\rho(\varphi,\psi)=\tau(\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi\text{-complement})=\tau(\neg(\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi))$. The solution instead uses
$$\rho_s(\varphi,\psi)=1-\tau_s(\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi).$$
These coincide only if $s(\neg e)=1-s(e)$ for all $e$ — an **involution/MV property** that holds on Łukasiewicz/MV algebras but **fails on Heyting algebras** (where $\neg$ is not an involution). Yet §7/§8 and Theorem "main" claim that "all these properties reduce to the classical $[0,1]$-valued ones" and that the construction recovers the Background verbatim, while simultaneously emphasizing Heyting examples ($M_2$, etc.).

**Required fix.** Either (i) restrict the "recovers the classical theory" claim to MV/Łukasiewicz $L$ where $s(\neg e)=1-s(e)$; or (ii) define $\rho_s$ via $\tau_s(\neg(\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi))$ to literally match the Background and re-verify the triangle inequality under that definition. As written, the literal-agreement claim is unjustified on the non-chain (Heyting) examples the paper highlights.
